messages:
caroline: Heads up — planning to publish Python & TS SDKs (py 0.42.0 / ts 0.42.0) during tonight's 23:00 UTC change window. Need agreement on pin strategy, canary length, and rollback criteria.
deploy-bot: Deploy window reserved for #devex at 2024-06-15 23:00 UTC. Use /deploy confirm to lock.
ben: Plan: canary to staging for 2 hours, smoke + integration tests. If any client-facing tests fail, we stop promote.
alice: Which tests are gating production? smoke, e2e against local emulator, checksum verify + signed artifacts.
emily: I'll run package signing & checksum verify pre-publish, ETA 22:30 UTC. I'll also upload artifacts to the internal staging bucket for QA.
caroline: Pinning proposal: announce deprecation of legacy sync client and pin examples to 0.31.x for now. For public instructions include explicit pinned install example: `pip install redwood==0.41.3` if they need a stable fallback.
dave: For TS, publish canary under `@redwood/sdk@next` first, then promote to `latest` after 2h if no regressions. Also bump peerDeps as discussed.
emily: Publish steps I'll run (copy for ops):
```
# python
python -m build
twine upload dist/* --sign --repository pypi
# TS
npm run build && npm publish --tag next
```
frank: Rollback options spelled out: PyPI -- yank package version + cut 0.42.1 patch with fix. NPM -- unpublish within 72h or immediately publish 0.42.1 patch and update docs. Do NOT attempt to re-upload exact same version on PyPI.
caroline: Agreed — policy is yank + patch for PyPI. For npm we can unpublish within the window but prefer new patch publish to avoid registry issues.
ben: Pin strategy for customers: add a short section in the release notes showing how to pin to previous stable (pip/npm) and include a troubleshooting snippet. Also prepare a short support playbook incase customers hit regressions.
alice: I'll write the support playbook bullets: how to detect, steps to pin, telemetry to collect (sdk version, request ids, sample prompts, token usage).
emily: I'll draft release notes now and paste here for review. Key callouts: breaking deprecations, migration snippet for async->new API, checksum & signing notes, and recommended pin. Link will be posted.
caroline: Monitoring/alert thresholds: if server-side error rate for SDK endpoints > 2% for 10m or client telemetry shows >3% failures in first 15m, we trigger rollback. Ben to monitor canary logs and Emily to watch publish pipeline.
frank: Emergency rollback runbook: 1) Pause promotions, 2) yank PyPI version, 3) publish 0.42.1 patch, 4) update status page + support message. Tag changelog with revert entry.
caroline: Also add a short CLI snippet in release notes showing pin and how to verify checksum: `pip install redwood==0.41.3 && pip hash redwood` and link to signed artifact in release assets.
emily: Draft ready: https://rwd.internal/release/0.42.0 (will update after publish). Please comment if anything missing.
dave: One more: run the internal generator test with 5k tokens for latency regression — if median latency increases >15% abort promotion.
ben: Noted. I'll run latency checks during the canary and post results.
caroline: Last question — do we want a short staged rollout (region by region) or global? I prefer staged (us-east -> eu -> apac).
frank: Staged is safer. We'll route a small % to us-east first and then increase.
emily: No objections. Publish confirmed for 23:00 UTC unless someone objects before 22:45.
deploy-bot: Publish window locked by caroline at 1718000000.
caroline: Locked. I'll kick off the canary at 23:00, monitor the first 15 minutes closely. If we see the thresholds trigger, we rollback per plan.
ben: I'll be on watch and will call rollback if needed.
alice: Support playbook & release notes ready to post after publish.
emily: Posting final notes to #eng-releases after the push. Link will include migration snippets and pin instructions.
frank: :thumbsup:
caroline: Thanks team — appreciate the quick sync.
